rv.q: From concept through execution A Devil Comes to Town is a haunting, surreal masterpiece, and a jewel in Trap Door Theatre’s crown that you don’t want to miss.
Indescribably good, really, “A Devil Comes To Town” comes highly recommended and has already had its run extended, playing through December 6 at Trap Door Theatre , 1655 W Cortland St in Chicago.
A Devil Comes to Town is occasionally puzzling but always engaging as long as you don’t demand that it make complete sense.
This one's funny because it's true.
The play is indeed obscure, in the sense of opaque and unilluminating, and also challenging, in the sense of tangled and unfathomable.
A Devil Comes to Town demonstrates Trap Door Theatre's fearless embrace of theatrical experimentation.

cn.t: Trap Door Theatre's adaptation earns praise for its mesmerizing storytelling and bold experimental style, though critics split on whether its inventive approach fully dramatizes the dark comedic tale of literary ambition and devilish deals.
